The Ulama and their dogmatic views do not fit in with our new and modern Egypt. The King is Zilullah fi'l-Ard, he reflects divine justice on Earth and the Ulama have time and time again gone against his judgement. They do not serve Allah, they serve only themselves and their allies abroad. They have outlived their purpose, it is time for them to §Rdie§!.

§RPurge the Burjwaziyyin§!

§RThis decision will purge the Burjwaziyyin faction, meaning that they cannot coup you. It also means that you won't be able to do any of the remaining Burjwaziyyin faction decisions. §GDecisions related to expansion and cores are unaffected.§! The Burjwaziyyin and their European ideals have been vital in modernizing our society and helping us become the strong regional power we are. However, with every demand and proposal they put forward it is becoming increasingly clear that they have not only acquired a European understanding of law and administration, but also of politics. It seems that their ultimate aim is to make the King nothing but a puppet of a parliament, denying his role as servant to Allah. It is best we §Rget rid of them§! before they get any revolutionary ideas.
The University of Cairo

The Burjwaziyyin have proposed that we approve the construction of a new university in Cairo. Their hope is that this institution will help further the modernisation of the country by increasing the literacy and education of the middle class.
Allow the Printing Press

The printing press is a technology created by the Europeans that allow for a much more efficient way to produce books. It has long been banned in Egypt because of the Ulama, who consider it sacrilege to print the words of the prophet with a machine. The Burjwaziyyin have recently asked us to lift this ban, so as to further increase the literacy in the country. The Ulama are of course staunchly against this, but they have offered no good alternative solution.
Outlaw the practice of slavery

Egypt has a long tradition of slavery. The ancient egyptians had slave trade, the mamluks who ruled the nation for hundreds of years were originally slaves, and we profit from the slave trade today. However, the Burjwaziyyin have started picking up on European values, and there slavery is nowadays seen as a blight on a nation and a moral wrongdoing. They have also mentioned that slavery creates a class system that blocks slaves from advancing and learning, depriving us of workers for the factories that come with the advent of industrilization. The Ulama and Nubala are opposed to ending the practice, but we must make a decision as Zilullah fi'l-Ard if we believe Allah would support slavery or not.
Enact Land Reform

The issue of land reform has been a hotly debated topic in Egypt for quite some time. The Burjwaziyyin argue that the current distribution of land keeps the commoners poor and thus outside of the state. By enacting a massive land reform we would integrate the common people into the state, giving them a stronger personal economy and importantly weakening the Ulama and Nubala by seizing part of their lands.
Establish a Parliament

The Burjwaziyyin have learnt of the way politics are handled in many European nations. The King does not rule with absolute power, but instead power is divided between the King and an elected body of representatives. The Burjwaziyyin are of course highly supportive of this idea, and it would let us weaken the power of the Ulama and Nubala by creating a more unified power structure in the country.
Enact Military Reforms

The Nubala are staunch admirers of the Umayyad Caliphate and their mastery of warfare. They have studied the European ways of fighting and found them far more advanced than our own, and wish for us to implement quite large reforms to adapt to new military innovations and tactics. The Burjwaziyyin are against this proposal, as they see it as a waste of resources, and the Ulama oppose it as they see it as a betrayal of the true Caliph.
Enact Naval Reforms

The Nubala have studied the naval structure and organization of nations like Venice and Aragon, and find them fascinating. They have started pushing for comprehensive naval reforms to form a more European style navy, and are supported by the trade hungry Burjwaziyyin in this endeavour. The Ulama oppose it due to the European nature of the reforms, but it cannot be denied that the reforms are needed if we wish to become a dominant power in the mediteranean.
Embrace Religious Law

The Ulama have started pushing for a more strict adherence to religious scripture in our legal system. We could implement it to appease them, but the Burjwaziyyin are staunchly against it, citing it as everything we are trying to get rid of with our sweeping reforms.
Enact the Pure Thoughts Act

The Ulama have declared our nation decadent and immoral. They cite our birthrates as proof that the nation has lost its way and have demanded that we implement more severe punishments for intercourse outside of marriage to save the nation from eternal damnation.
Enact tight Censorship
The Ulama have demanded that we enact strong censorship laws to punish those who spread blasphemy and dangerous ideas.
Revert the Censorship laws

The strong censorship laws we enacted were always a bad idea, and removing them would benefit the entire nation. The Ulama will of course be annoyed if we do such a thing, but we cannot let the nation be dominated by the ideas of old men. It is a new century that requires new ideas.
Strengthen Royal Authority

We can improve the power of the crown by using those loyal to the king in the different factions to strengthen our hand in negotiations. §GThis decision gives you 2 central authority and has a 3 year long cooldown. Once you have 10 central authority you can purge a faction of your choosing.§!
